name: Runner Extras - Object Metadata System Table
brief: Issue #2519: Object Metadata (2000000071) is a real application-database table, not a virtual one. The runner has no application database, so it synthesises the row set from BC's own SystemTables.ApplicationDatabaseTables and leaves the compiled-metadata payload columns blank. This suite pins the synthesis and the blank payload so neither can change silently.
description: What Object Metadata CONTAINS - one row per application-database system table, Object Type = Table, nothing else - is plain BC behaviour and BELONGS upstream, but could not go there and is NOT service-tier-adjudicated. Corpus PR StefanMaron/BusinessCentral.AL.Language.Tests#153 was withdrawn after all 8 BC legs of run 33968379281 refused the only route a Cloud-target app has: the record type does not compile (AL0296, the table is Scope = OnPrem) and RecordRef.Open is refused at runtime by NavRecordRef.CheckIsOpenAllowed, because 2000000071 is in SystemTables.InternalTables. The row set the runner synthesises is therefore derived from Microsoft's own publish-side code - the insert predicate in InPlacePublisher.UpsertIntoMetadataStorageImpl - and is an upper bound, not a confirmed equality; see the header of AlRunner/Patches/RecordPatches.ObjectMetadataSystemTable.cs for what is open. This suite therefore pins what the RUNNER does, which is what a runner suite is for: that the rows appear at all with no application database behind them, that the ids track BC's own list, that the compiled-metadata payload columns (Metadata, User Code, User AL Code, Symbol Reference, Metadata Version, Hash, Object Subtype, Has Subscribers, Schema Hash) read blank rather than carrying a fabricated payload, and that Emit Version is a real BC build emit version rather than a chosen constant. The blank payload is a DECLARED divergence, recorded in docs/limitations.md; issue #2771 tracks making those columns refuse by name instead, which needs a per-field blob-read seam the shared TempTableDataProvider path does not have. Target is OnPrem, not Cloud: Microsoft declares Object Metadata Scope = OnPrem, so an AL object naming the record type cannot compile for Cloud (AL0296).
